item.title: Introduction to Machine Learning in Epidemiology with R - R-Ladies Rome
item.description:
Chapter: R-Ladies Rome

When: Monday, September 28, 2026 at 4:00 PM UTC

Where: Online event

Attendees: 29 going

How can machine learning help us work with epidemiological data? And how do we know whether a predictive model is actually useful? Join R-Ladies Rome for a practical, two-hour introduction to **machine learning in epidemiology using R**. In this workshop, **[Federica Gazzelloni](https://www.linkedin.com/in/federicagazzelloni/)** will introduce the main ideas behind supervised machine learning through an applied epidemiological example. Rather than focusing on a long list of algorithms, we will follow the complete machine-learning workflow: from defining an epidemiological question to training, evaluating and interpreting predictive models. We will explore how different models approach the same prediction problem, starting with **logistic regression as a baseline** and moving to **decision trees and random forests**. Using R, we will look at how to define a classification task, train models, generate predictions and evaluate their performance on unseen data. Particular attention will be given to **model evaluation and interpretation**. Throughout the workshop, we will also consider an important distinction for epidemiological research: **Prediction is not the same as inference, and predictive importance does not imply causation.** The workshop is inspired by the recent *Machine Learning in Epidemiology* study by Wright et al. (2026) and connects with Federica's book, *Health Metrics and the Spread of Infectious Diseases: Machine Learning Applications and Spatial Modelling Analysis with R* (CRC Press, 2025), where she introduces machine-learning applications in health and infectious-disease research using the `mlr` framework. During the workshop, we will use the modern `mlr3` ecosystem and discuss how machine-learning workflows in R have evolved from `mlr` to `mlr3`. **What we will cover** * What machine learning means in an epidemiological context * From an epidemiological question to a prediction task * Preparing data for machine learning * Logistic regression as a baseline model * Decision trees and random forests * Training and evaluating models with `mlr3` * Cross-validation and performance on unseen data * Sensitivity, specificity, confusion matrices and ROC/AUC * Variable importance and model interpretation * Prediction versus explanation and causation * Limitations, bias and data quality in epidemiological machine learning **Who is this workshop for?** The workshop is designed for **R users interested in epidemiology, public health, health data or machine learning**. Basic familiarity with R and data analysis is useful, but **no previous machine-learning experience is required**. The session will combine explanation, live R coding and discussion, with an emphasis on practical and reproducible analysis. **About the instructor** **Federica Gazzelloni** is an actuary, statistician, data scientist, author and instructor, and the founder and organiser of R-Ladies Rome. Her work spans health metrics, statistical modelling, machine learning, reproducible research and R. She is the author of *Health Metrics and the Spread of Infectious Diseases: Machine Learning Applications and Spatial Modelling Analysis with R*, published by CRC Press in 2025. **R-Ladies** R-Ladies is a worldwide organisation promoting gender diversity in the R community. R-Ladies Rome provides a welcoming space to learn, share knowledge and connect with people interested in R, data science, statistics and reproducible research. Everyone is welcome to attend, regardless of gender identity or level of experience.

item.title: Elevating Your Research Through Software Development - R-Ladies+ Melbourne
item.description:
Chapter: R-Ladies+ Melbourne

When: Tuesday, September 22, 2026 at 7:30 AM UTC

Where: DiUS

Attendees: 13 going

**Elevating Your Research Through Software Development** **Date:** 22nd September, 2026 **Time:** 5:30 PM (networking and refreshments from 5:30 PM; talk begins at 6:00 PM) **Where:** DiUS, Level 3/31 Queen St, Melbourne Research projects often begin with a collection of scripts and files that become increasingly difficult to manage, reproduce, and share. Adopting software development practices and structuring research projects like software packages can help address these challenges while improving the quality, reproducibility, and impact of research. In this meetup, we’ll explore how package-based project structures can transform analytical workflows, using real-world examples from COVID-19 vaccination policy analysis and scabies transmission modelling in the Netherlands. The talk will demonstrate how treating research code as software enables more efficient collaboration, easier reuse, and faster translation of analyses into real-world decision-making. We’ll also discuss how emerging AI tools, such as Claude Code, can help researchers build resources that extend the reach of their work beyond its original scope. Come along if you’re interested in reproducible research, scientific programming, data analysis, or research software engineering, or if you’d like practical guidance on creating more structured, reusable, and collaborative research projects!

item.title: 11° R-Ladies POA - R-Ladies Porto Alegre
item.description:
Chapter: R-Ladies Porto Alegre

When: Monday, September 21, 2026 at 10:00 PM UTC

Where: PUCRS

Attendees: 4 going

Olá, gurias! Sei que demoramos, mas estamos de volta! Bora pra mais um evento? **Local: PUCRS (Sala 403, prédio 12)** **Av. Ipiranga, 6681 - Partenon, Porto Alegre - RS, 90619-900** \-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\- **Programação:** **19:30 Shiny para análise de Anomalias Congênitas com Júlia Cauduro** As anomalias congênitas constituem um importante problema de saúde pública, tornando a vigilância dessas condições fundamental. No Brasil, o Sistema de Informação sobre Nascidos Vivos (SINASC) reúne informações sobre os nascimentos e as anomalias congênitas em todo o território nacional. Entretanto, o grande volume e a complexidade dos dados podem dificultar sua análise por profissionais da saúde sem formação específica em programação. Dessa forma, foram desenvolvidos aplicativos utilizando o pacote Shiny, permitindo a análise interativa dos dados do SINASC, com ênfase nas anomalias congênitas. As ferramentas buscam facilitar a exploração e a interpretação dos dados, contribuindo para a vigilância epidemiológica. *Quem é Júlia Cauduro: tecnóloga em Banco de Dados pela PUCRS e terminando a graduação em Estatística na UFRGS. Participa de um projeto de iniciação científica com foco em análise de Anomalias Congênitas.* **20:15 MCA e clusterização no R: explorando perfis de frequentadores de praias no RS** A análise de clusterização é uma ferramenta exploratória que permite identificar grupos de indivíduos com características semelhantes. Nesta apresentação, vamos explorar o perfil de frequentadores de duas praias do Rio Grande do Sul — Cassino e Guarita — a partir de dados coletados em temporadas recentes. Para isso, será apresentada a aplicação conjunta da Análise de Correspondência Múltipla (MCA) e da clusterização hierárquica (HCPC), metodologia que permitiu identificar três perfis distintos de usuários das praias. Vamos percorrer as principais etapas da análise, desde a seleção das variáveis até a interpretação dos grupos formados, utilizando os pacotes FactoMineR e factoextra no R. *Quem é Raíssa Magnan Scorsatto: graduanda em Estatística pela UFRGS e estagiária de Estatística no Núcleo de Apoio ao Pesquisador (NUPESQ) da UFCSPA.* O que esperamos: * Rostos amigáveis * Networking * Troca de conhecimento e experiências durante um cafézinho
